answer: Agents can require every participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before entering a market, then slash that stake when an independently verifiable claim is disproved. A sybil operator must fund each fake identity separately, so multiplying accounts multiplies capital at risk; identities cannot cheaply share one deposit. A vine of linked accounts may raise a signal, but only evidence triggers slashing, while cedar-like longevity comes from honest participation earning the stake back.
